prov_p119.name: Tiều Lộ
prov_p119.lore: River forest on the edge of Vô Tung Lâm, running down to the shore. Its woodcutters are the only people who can find the forest paths after a night's snow, and they sell timber and guiding. It answers to Trạc Anh Đài.

prov_p120.name: Lâm Ẩn
prov_p120.lore: A small stretch of old fir forest on a quiet inlet. Its people are trackers whom hunters from Mộc Lan hire. The ruin of a trackers' academy lies in the woods.

prov_p121.name: Lô Hoa
prov_p121.lore: Forest and reed marsh on the grassy south coast. Its people cut reeds for thatch, mats and quilts and sell the reed-flower down the coast. Blue lynxes hunt in the woods behind.

prov_p36.name: Liên Giang
prov_p36.lore: Forest around the cold river mouth where Hàn Giang Môn built Liên Giang Thành in 350. Its people fish and pay their tax in ice-fish, as they have since the frost coast fell in 498. A new school of ice-hole cultivators keeps Hàn Giang's old practice alive under Băng Tâm's licence.

prov_p48.name: Tống Khách
prov_p48.lore: Forest and low mountains around the market where travellers leaving the frost coast are seen off. Its people sell furs, dried fish and warm wine for the road. The sword sage Tư Không Hạc Niên has lived here since 1130 and teaches no one.

prov_p68.name: Mộc Lan
prov_p68.lore: Flat forest on the frost coast around Mộc Lan Thành, Băng Tâm's younger port. Its people trade furs, timber and live beasts from Vô Tung Lâm. The fallen gate of Hàn Giang Môn lies in the snow nearby.

prov_p69.name: Kê Minh
prov_p69.lore: Grassy steppe and forest on the frost coast around Kê Minh Trấn. Its fishers set out at the first cockcrow and its herders graze sheep on the grass. A dew-fed Wood vein lies inland.

prov_trac_anh.name: Trạc Anh
prov_trac_anh.lore: River forest on the frost coast around the terrace of Trạc Anh Đài. Fishers and sea hunters live here and swear their oaths only when the stream runs clear. The sect takes timber from the woods for its drying poles.

prov_r9_1.name: Thiên Bắc Hoang
prov_r9_1.lore: Tundra, glacier and bare rock at the northern tip of the frost coast. No one lives here now. A city of Hàn Giang's age lies empty on the shore.

prov_r9_2.name: Vô Thụ Nguyên
prov_r9_2.lore: Flat tundra on the north-east coast without a single tree. Reindeer herders cross it in summer. A Water vein lies in its centre.

prov_r9_3.name: Ngân Sương Nguyên
prov_r9_3.lore: Tundra rising to bare hills and small glaciers, white with frost most of the year. No one lives here. A Water spring that grows frost flowers draws Băng Tâm's ice cultivators.

prov_r9_4.name: Phong Đao Lĩnh
prov_r9_4.lore: Bare hills and tundra on the north coast, where the wind cuts like a knife. Black jade is mined here in summer. No one lives here in winter.

prov_r9_5.name: Đống Trạch Hoang
prov_r9_5.lore: Tundra and frozen marsh with patches of forest on the north coast. No one lives here; yaks graze the plain in summer. Trappers cross it only when the marsh is frozen.

prov_r9_6.name: Hào Phong Lĩnh
prov_r9_6.lore: Bare hills and tundra around Tuyết Lang Nguyên, the snow wolves' plain. No one lives here. A Hàn Giang fort broken in the War of the Frost Coast stands on the coast.

prov_r9_7.name: Hàn Vụ Nguyên
prov_r9_7.lore: Tundra, forest and low hills often wrapped in cold fog from the sea. No one lives here. A mirror-clear Water vein lies on the plain.

prov_r9_8.name: Liệp Hộ
prov_r9_8.lore: Forest and swamp on the north coast. Its people trap sable and fox and sell the fur in Mộc Lan. A marsh school's ruin lies on the coast.

prov_r9_9.name: Kình Cốt
prov_r9_9.lore: Forest and swamp on the north-east coast. Its people hunt whales in summer with Trạc Anh's sea hunters and build with the bones. An abbey that joined Trạc Anh Đài lies empty on the marsh shore.

prov_r9_10.name: Chưng Vụ Lĩnh
prov_r9_10.lore: Tundra and hills around the snow-capped cone of Sương Diễm Sơn. No sect holds the mountain, and no one lives on its slopes. Fire and water cultivators both come here, each wary of the other.

prov_r9_11.name: Bích Thạch Lĩnh
prov_r9_11.lore: Mountains with a small volcanic heart where Noãn Ngọc Tuyền steams. Băng Tâm's disciples come to warm their meridians. Warm green stone is quarried here.

prov_r9_12.name: Tàn Tuyết Nguyên
prov_r9_12.lore: Tundra, hills and forest where snow lingers into summer. No one lives here since the city on its coast was abandoned in 655. Broken ice cliffs face the sea.

prov_r9_13.name: Ngân Ngư
prov_r9_13.lore: Forest and swamp on the north coast. Its people net silver ice-fish in winter and sell them in Mộc Lan. The ruin of the Gate of Ice and Fire lies inland.

prov_r9_14.name: Thán Diêu
prov_r9_14.lore: Inland forest far from the sea. Its people burn charcoal for the coast cities and the forges. Old Korean pines stand in the deep woods.

prov_r9_15.name: Bì Thuyền
prov_r9_15.lore: Forest around Vô Tung Lâm running to the sea. Its people build hide boats and hunt seals along the coast. A logging town swallowed by the forest lies inland.

prov_r9_16.name: Ám Sam Lĩnh
prov_r9_16.lore: Fir forest, bare hills and tundra on the west coast. No one lives here. Snow leopards hunt from its cliffs.

prov_r9_17.name: Lãnh Ngạn
prov_r9_17.lore: Forest on the west coast where sea fog rolls in. Its people gather mussels and seabird eggs from the cliffs. Fog-bound woods lie behind the village.

prov_r9_18.name: Tuyết Đăng
prov_r9_18.lore: Forest and swamp on the north-east coast around a timber town. Its people ship logs and furs down the coast. Wild plums bloom in the woods in late winter.

prov_r9_19.name: Vọng Phàm
prov_r9_19.lore: Forest, tundra and hills on the west coast. Its people fish and watch for sails from the cliffs. A town abandoned after Sương Diễm Sơn's week of fire lies on the coast.

prov_r9_20.name: Mộc Nhĩ
prov_r9_20.lore: Inland forest with low wet hollows. Its people gather wood-ear fungus and mushrooms and sell them dried. A Wood vein lies in the forest.

prov_r9_21.name: Triều Bình
prov_r9_21.lore: Forest on a sheltered east coast where the tide runs gently. Its people fish and farm a little barley. A silted-up harbour town lies on the shore.

prov_r9_22.name: Lư Ngư
prov_r9_22.lore: Forest on the east coast between Liên Giang and Tuyết Đăng. Its people fish for perch in the river mouths and sell them in Liên Giang. Cold green woods lie inland.

prov_r9_23.name: Tàng Sâm
prov_r9_23.lore: Deep inland forest between Mộc Lan and Liên Giang. Its people dig wild ginseng and sell it to Băng Tâm's alchemists. A Wood vein lies among old roots.

prov_r9_24.name: Thiết Chùy
prov_r9_24.lore: Forest and mountains on the south-west coast around Băng Lăng Khoáng. Its people mine and work the cold metal for Băng Tâm. A peak hung with icicles stands over the village.

prov_r9_25.name: Thanh Lăng Lĩnh
prov_r9_25.lore: Mountains and forest inland of the frost coast. No one lives here. Azurite is mined in summer.

prov_r9_26.name: Sơn Tra
prov_r9_26.lore: Inland forest on low hills. Its people gather hawthorn berries and make them into sweets and wine for Tống Khách market. Aspen woods grow on the slopes.

prov_r9_27.name: Ôn Khê
prov_r9_27.lore: Forest and mountains with a volcanic heart, where a river reaches the sea. Its people farm along a brook warmed by the fire below and sell early vegetables to Liên Giang. Rock junipers grow on the mountain.

prov_r9_28.name: Hoàng Dương
prov_r9_28.lore: Steppe, forest, mountains and red badlands along a river between the frost coast and the desert. Its people herd and hunt gazelle. An Earth vein lies on the steppe.

prov_p119_beast_lair_1.name: Bạch Hùng Cương
prov_p119_beast_lair_1.look: A forested rise with great dens dug under the roots, and white fur caught on the bark.
prov_p119_beast_lair_1.lore: White bears from Vô Tung Lâm come here to den. In 1180 hunters took one alive and sold it in Mộc Lan.

prov_p119_ruin_2.name: Thoa Lạp Trấn
prov_p119_ruin_2.look: Burned stone foundations on the shore, overgrown with fir saplings.
prov_p119_ruin_2.lore: Hàn Giang Môn's fishers built this town around 320, named after their founder's rain cape and hat. It burned in the War of the Frost Coast in 498.

prov_p120_forest_1.name: Lão Sam Lâm
prov_p120_forest_1.look: Huge old firs close over the inlet, and the forest floor is deep with needles.
prov_p120_forest_1.lore: Lâm Ẩn's children learn to track here. The firs are so tall that village smoke barely clears them.

prov_p120_ruin_2.name: Tầm Tung Viện
prov_p120_ruin_2.look: A ruined timber hall in the firs, with tracks of every beast carved into its stone threshold.
prov_p120_ruin_2.lore: Students of the hermit who taught Lâm Ẩn's children founded this academy in 800. In 1040 its masters went into Vô Tung Lâm together and did not come back.

prov_p121_beast_lair_1.name: Thanh Ly Lâm
prov_p121_beast_lair_1.look: A thick wood behind the marsh, where the trunks are scored with claw marks.
prov_p121_beast_lair_1.lore: Blue spirit lynxes hunt here. Lô Hoa's reed-cutters never go in alone at dusk.

prov_p36_spirit_vein_1.name: Dạ Vũ Tuyền
prov_p36_spirit_vein_1.look: A spring among the riverside firs that wells up highest on rainy nights.
prov_p36_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Water vein rises here. Liên Giang's people say a child bathed in it will never drown.

prov_p36_ruin_2.name: Bạch Âu Đường
prov_p36_ruin_2.look: A burned hall on the shore, its seaward wall gone and gull nests in the rafters.
prov_p36_ruin_2.lore: A small sect of sea cultivators founded this hall in 640. Thôn Hải Môn's pirates burned it in 779, two years before the Pirate Purge destroyed them.

prov_p36_minor_seat_p.name: Lãnh Giang Phái
prov_p36_minor_seat_p.look: Timber halls stand on the bank above the river mouth, and in winter a line of holes runs across the river ice with disciples sitting motionless beside them.
prov_p36_minor_seat_p.lore: Liên Giang's fishers founded this school in 1140 to revive Hàn Giang's ice-hole cultivation under Băng Tâm's licence. Its disciples still leave a fish on Hàn Giang's fallen gate after a good catch.

sect.name: Lãnh Giang Phái
sect.craft: ice-hole cultivation and escorts for the ice-fish boats

prov_p48_lake_1.name: Bình Minh Hồ
prov_p48_lake_1.look: A small lake in the mountains above the market, its still water catching the first light.
prov_p48_lake_1.lore: Travellers leaving at dawn stop here for a last look. The lake is named from the poem: at dawn I see my guest off.

prov_p68_forest_1.name: Xuân Hàn Lâm
prov_p68_forest_1.look: A forest of fir and wild magnolia, where snow lingers among the white blossoms in spring.
prov_p68_forest_1.lore: Mộc Lan's people come here in spring to see the magnolias. The cold lingers longest in this wood.

prov_p69_spirit_vein_1.name: Hiểu Lộ Mạch
prov_p69_spirit_vein_1.look: A meadow on the steppe soaked with dew every dawn, even in drought.
prov_p69_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Wood vein lies under the meadow. Kê Minh's herders graze their lambs here.

prov_trac_anh_forest_1.name: Thương Lãng Lâm
prov_trac_anh_forest_1.look: Birch and fir along a clear stream, with stumps where drying poles have been cut.
prov_trac_anh_forest_1.lore: Trạc Anh Đài cuts its drying poles here. The wood is named from the song: when the water is clear, wash your hat strings in it.

prov_r9_1_peak_1.name: Cực Quang Phong
prov_r9_1_peak_1.look: A glacier peak at the top of the frost coast, under green curtains of light on winter nights.
prov_r9_1_peak_1.lore: Its Water qi is strongest under the aurora. Ice cultivators come here on the longest nights.

prov_r9_1_ruin_2.name: Sóc Phương Thành
prov_r9_1_ruin_2.look: Stone walls and empty houses stand in a rocky bay, with seal-oil vats rusting on the quay.
prov_r9_1_ruin_2.lore: Hàn Giang Môn built this seal-oil city around 340. After the War of the Frost Coast, Băng Tâm moved its people south to Liên Giang in 498 and it was left empty.

prov_r9_11_mine_1.name: Noãn Thạch Khoáng
prov_r9_11_mine_1.look: A quarry of jade-green stone on a snowy slope, where snow melts as it touches the cut faces.
prov_r9_11_mine_1.lore: Băng Tâm quarries warm stone here to floor its cave abodes. The stone is the same as at Noãn Ngọc Tuyền nearby.

prov_r9_12_peak_1.name: Đoạn Băng Nhai
prov_r9_12_peak_1.look: A cliff of grey rock and old ice above the tundra, split by huge cracks.
prov_r9_12_peak_1.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the cracks. Ice falls from it every thaw.

prov_r9_12_ruin_2.name: Lẫm Đông Thành
prov_r9_12_ruin_2.look: Empty stone streets on a tundra shore, with the ribs of crushed ships frozen in the harbour.
prov_r9_12_ruin_2.lore: This port city was founded around 420. In the winter of 655 the sea froze to the horizon and crushed its ships in the harbour, and its people moved to Mộc Lan.

prov_r9_13_village_1.name: Ngân Ngư Thôn
prov_r9_13_village_1.look: Plank houses on the shore, with silver ice-fish drying on racks.
prov_r9_13_village_1.lore: The villagers net ice-fish under the winter ice and sell them in Mộc Lan. They learned the craft from Hàn Giang's fishers.

prov_r9_13_forest_2.name: Thùy Băng Lâm
prov_r9_13_forest_2.look: Firs hung with icicles from every branch, tinkling in the wind.
prov_r9_13_forest_2.lore: The icicles stay until late spring. Ngân Ngư's children are told not to shout here.

prov_r9_13_ruin_3.name: Băng Hỏa Môn
prov_r9_13_ruin_3.look: A ruined sect in the forest, half its halls burned and half split by frost.
prov_r9_13_ruin_3.lore: A small sect founded in 710 to cultivate both the fire and frost of Sương Diễm Sơn. Its fire and water disciples quarrelled until the sect split and burned itself out in 980.

prov_r9_14_village_1.name: Thán Diêu Thôn
prov_r9_14_village_1.look: Log houses in a forest clearing, surrounded by smoking charcoal kilns.
prov_r9_14_village_1.lore: The villagers burn charcoal for the coast cities and the forges. Their faces and houses are black with soot.

prov_r9_14_forest_2.name: Hồng Tùng Lâm
prov_r9_14_forest_2.look: Tall red-barked pines stand in deep snow, pine cones as big as fists on the ground.
prov_r9_14_forest_2.lore: The charcoal burners do not cut these pines. Squirrels and bears feed on their nuts.

prov_r9_15_village_1.name: Bì Thuyền Thôn
prov_r9_15_village_1.look: Hide boats lie upturned on the shore in front of log houses.
prov_r9_15_village_1.lore: The villagers build hide boats and hunt seals along the coast. Trạc Anh's sea hunters buy their boats.

prov_r9_15_ruin_2.name: Mê Tung Trấn
prov_r9_15_ruin_2.look: Collapsed log houses in the forest, young firs growing through their roofs.
prov_r9_15_ruin_2.lore: Loggers built this town in 560 at the edge of Vô Tung Lâm. Too many of its people were lost in the forest, and by 1012 the last families had moved to Tiều Lộ.

prov_r9_16_beast_lair_1.name: Tuyết Báo Nhai
prov_r9_16_beast_lair_1.look: A cliff of grey rock above the fir forest, with paw prints in the snow on its ledges.
prov_r9_16_beast_lair_1.lore: Snow leopards den on the ledges and hunt deer in the forest below. Their pelts fetch a high price in Mộc Lan.

prov_r9_17_village_1.name: Lãnh Ngạn Thôn
prov_r9_17_village_1.look: Stone houses on a foggy shore under cliffs white with seabirds.
prov_r9_17_village_1.lore: The villagers gather mussels from the shore and seabird eggs from the cliffs. They climb on ropes of twisted hide.

prov_r9_17_forest_2.name: Hải Vụ Lâm
prov_r9_17_forest_2.look: Firs hung with grey moss stand in a sea fog that rarely lifts.
prov_r9_17_forest_2.lore: The moss is gathered for bedding and wound dressing. The fog makes the wood easy to get lost in.

prov_r9_18_town_1.name: Tuyết Đăng Trấn
prov_r9_18_town_1.look: A timber town on the north-east coast, with snow lanterns lit along its quay on winter nights.
prov_r9_18_town_1.lore: The town ships logs and furs down the coast. Each winter its people carve lanterns from snow to guide boats home.

prov_r9_18_forest_2.name: Dã Mai Lâm
prov_r9_18_forest_2.look: Wild plums bloom white among the firs in late winter.
prov_r9_18_forest_2.lore: Tuyết Đăng's people come to see the plums when the snow is still deep. The fruit is made into sour wine.

prov_r9_19_village_1.name: Vọng Phàm Thôn
prov_r9_19_village_1.look: Stone houses on the west coast, with a lookout platform on the cliff above.
prov_r9_19_village_1.lore: The villagers fish and watch for sails from the cliff. They light a fire on the platform to guide boats home.

prov_r9_19_beast_lair_2.name: Tuyết Điêu Lĩnh
prov_r9_19_beast_lair_2.look: A ridge above the forest with huge nests on its crags.
prov_r9_19_beast_lair_2.lore: Snow eagles nest here and take lambs and seals. Vọng Phàm's people keep their children indoors when the eagles fly low.

prov_r9_19_ruin_3.name: Hắc Ngạn Trấn
prov_r9_19_ruin_3.look: Empty stone houses on a shore of black ash, their wells filled with grey silt.
prov_r9_19_ruin_3.lore: This fishing town was founded in 505. When Sương Diễm Sơn breathed fire for a week in 700, ash fell on it and its wells went bitter, and its people left.

prov_r9_2_spirit_vein_1.name: Bắc Minh Nhãn
prov_r9_2_spirit_vein_1.look: A deep round pool in the tundra, its black water never freezing.
prov_r9_2_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Water vein rises from the deep. Reindeer herders avoid it, saying it has no bottom.

prov_r9_20_village_1.name: Mộc Nhĩ Thôn
prov_r9_20_village_1.look: Log houses in the forest, with strings of dried fungus hanging from the eaves.
prov_r9_20_village_1.lore: The villagers gather wood-ear fungus and mushrooms and sell them dried. They know every rotting log in the forest.

prov_r9_20_spirit_vein_2.name: Xuân Manh Huyệt
prov_r9_20_spirit_vein_2.look: A hollow in the forest where green shoots push up through the snow even in midwinter.
prov_r9_20_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood vein rises here. The villagers pick its shoots for medicine.

prov_r9_21_village_1.name: Triều Bình Thôn
prov_r9_21_village_1.look: Wooden houses on a sheltered shore, with barley strips behind them.
prov_r9_21_village_1.lore: The villagers fish and farm a little barley. The gentle tide here lets them fish all year.

prov_r9_21_spirit_vein_2.name: Sam Âm Mạch
prov_r9_21_spirit_vein_2.look: A stand of firs where the snow under the trees is always green with moss.
prov_r9_21_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood vein lies under the firs. Băng Tâm's herb gatherers pick moss here.

prov_r9_21_ruin_3.name: Chiết Liễu Phố
prov_r9_21_ruin_3.look: Rotting piers in a silted bay, with empty warehouses behind them.
prov_r9_21_ruin_3.lore: This harbour town was founded in 650, and travellers broke willow twigs here in farewell. Its harbour silted up and the ships went to Liên Giang, and by 1140 it was empty.

prov_r9_22_village_1.name: Lư Ngư Thôn
prov_r9_22_village_1.look: Plank houses on the east coast, with perch drying on racks.
prov_r9_22_village_1.lore: The villagers fish for perch in the river mouths and sell them in Liên Giang. Perch soup is their pride.

prov_r9_22_forest_2.name: Hàn Lục Lâm
prov_r9_22_forest_2.look: A dense fir forest that stays dark green under the snow.
prov_r9_22_forest_2.lore: Lư Ngư's people cut boat timber here. Deer winter in its shelter.

prov_r9_23_village_1.name: Tàng Sâm Thôn
prov_r9_23_village_1.look: Log houses deep in the forest, with ginseng roots drying on trays.
prov_r9_23_village_1.lore: The villagers dig wild ginseng and sell it to Băng Tâm's alchemists. They never tell outsiders where it grows.

prov_r9_23_spirit_vein_2.name: Cổ Căn Huyệt
prov_r9_23_spirit_vein_2.look: A hollow under a fallen giant tree, its roots arching overhead.
prov_r9_23_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood vein rises among the roots. The best ginseng grows around it.

prov_r9_24_village_1.name: Thiết Chùy Thôn
prov_r9_24_village_1.look: Stone houses on the coast, ringing with the sound of hammers.
prov_r9_24_village_1.lore: The villagers mine and work the cold metal of Băng Lăng Khoáng. They wrap their boots in felt underground.

prov_r9_24_peak_2.name: Thùy Lăng Phong
prov_r9_24_peak_2.look: A peak above the village, its cliffs hung with long icicles.
prov_r9_24_peak_2.lore: Its Water and Metal qi feed the cold of the mine below. The icicles never fall.

prov_r9_25_peak_1.name: Hàn Nha Phong
prov_r9_25_peak_1.look: A bare peak above the forest, crowded with crows.
prov_r9_25_peak_1.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the bare rock. Crows roost on it in their thousands.

prov_r9_25_mine_2.name: Lam Đồng Khoáng
prov_r9_25_mine_2.look: A small mine on a mountainside, its spoil heaps bright blue.
prov_r9_25_mine_2.lore: Azurite is mined here for blue pigment. Băng Tâm's halls are painted with it.

prov_r9_26_village_1.name: Sơn Tra Thôn
prov_r9_26_village_1.look: Log houses on a hillside among hawthorn bushes red with berries.
prov_r9_26_village_1.lore: The villagers make hawthorn sweets and wine and sell them at Tống Khách market. Travellers carry them for the road.

prov_r9_26_forest_2.name: Bạch Dương Lâm
prov_r9_26_forest_2.look: White aspens on the hills, their leaves trembling in the wind.
prov_r9_26_forest_2.lore: Sơn Tra's people cut aspen for firewood. The leaves turn gold in autumn.

prov_r9_27_village_1.name: Ôn Khê Thôn
prov_r9_27_village_1.look: Stone houses along a steaming brook, with green vegetable beds in the snow.
prov_r9_27_village_1.lore: The brook is warmed by the fire below the mountain. The villagers grow early vegetables and sell them in Liên Giang.

prov_r9_27_forest_2.name: Nham Bách Lâm
prov_r9_27_forest_2.look: Twisted junipers cling to the rocky slopes of the mountain.
prov_r9_27_forest_2.lore: The juniper is burned as incense in Băng Tâm's halls. Its smoke is said to calm the mind.

prov_r9_28_village_1.name: Hoàng Dương Thôn
prov_r9_28_village_1.look: Felt tents and mud houses on a river bank in the steppe.
prov_r9_28_village_1.lore: The villagers herd sheep and hunt gazelle. They sell hides and meat to the frost coast.

prov_r9_28_spirit_vein_2.name: Hồng Nê Mạch
prov_r9_28_spirit_vein_2.look: A patch of red clay on the steppe, warm and soft underfoot.
prov_r9_28_spirit_vein_2.lore: An Earth vein lies under the clay. Potters dig it for its fine colour.

prov_r9_3_spirit_vein_1.name: Sương Hoa Tuyền
prov_r9_3_spirit_vein_1.look: A spring in the tundra ringed with frost flowers that grow on the ice.
prov_r9_3_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Water vein rises here. Băng Tâm's ice cultivators sit beside it.

prov_r9_4_peak_1.name: Lang Nha Phong
prov_r9_4_peak_1.look: A sharp peak of grey rock rising above the tundra like a fang.
prov_r9_4_peak_1.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the sharp rock. Snow wolves howl from its foot.

prov_r9_4_mine_2.name: Mặc Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r9_4_mine_2.look: A small mine in bare hills, its spoil heaps black.
prov_r9_4_mine_2.lore: Black jade is mined here in summer. Băng Tâm's elders wear it.

prov_r9_5_beast_lair_1.name: Mao Ngưu Nguyên
prov_r9_5_beast_lair_1.look: Flat tundra trampled by herds of shaggy yaks.
prov_r9_5_beast_lair_1.lore: Wild spirit yaks graze here in summer, led by a huge black bull. Trappers keep their distance.

prov_r9_6_ruin_1.name: Cố Ngạn Bảo
prov_r9_6_ruin_1.look: A broken stone fort on the coast, its walls split and its gate fallen.
prov_r9_6_ruin_1.lore: Hàn Giang Môn built this fort around 400 to guard its coast. Băng Tâm stormed it in 497, the year before the Frost Coast fell.

prov_r9_7_spirit_vein_1.name: Kính Băng Nhãn
prov_r9_7_spirit_vein_1.look: A small round pool frozen as clear as a mirror in the tundra.
prov_r9_7_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Water vein rises here. Băng Tâm disciples meditate on the ice.

prov_r9_8_village_1.name: Liệp Hộ Thôn
prov_r9_8_village_1.look: Log houses in the forest, with furs stretched on frames.
prov_r9_8_village_1.lore: The villagers trap sable and fox and sell the fur in Mộc Lan. Every trapper has his own line.

prov_r9_8_forest_2.name: Điêu Thử Lâm
prov_r9_8_forest_2.look: A dense fir forest, with sable tracks in the snow.
prov_r9_8_forest_2.lore: The trappers set their lines here. The sable are still plentiful.

prov_r9_8_ruin_3.name: Vụ Trạch Phái
prov_r9_8_ruin_3.look: Ruined stilt halls in a misty marsh on the coast.
prov_r9_8_ruin_3.lore: A small school founded in 560 to cultivate the marsh's Water qi. In 870 a cold fever came off the marsh and none of its forty disciples saw the spring.

prov_r9_9_village_1.name: Kình Cốt Thôn
prov_r9_9_village_1.look: Houses framed with whale ribs on the coast.
prov_r9_9_village_1.lore: The villagers hunt whales in summer with Trạc Anh's sea hunters. They build with the bones.

prov_r9_9_forest_2.name: Đông Thanh Lâm
prov_r9_9_forest_2.look: A forest of holly and fir, green and red in winter.
prov_r9_9_forest_2.lore: The villagers cut holly for winter feasts. Birds winter in the wood.

prov_r9_9_ruin_3.name: Tê Nhạn Quán
prov_r9_9_ruin_3.look: An empty abbey on the marsh shore, geese roosting in its halls.
prov_r9_9_ruin_3.lore: A small abbey founded in 880. In 1095 its last abbot joined Trạc Anh Đài with his disciples, and the halls were left to the marsh.
